subject.title: fix(cli-runner): assemble context engine before prompt on generic CLI hosts

question: Should generic CLI backends advertise full `assemble-before-prompt` support, or should OpenClaw keep that capability limited to hosts that can project assembled messages and metadata?
rationale: The PR changes a context-engine host capability contract that plugin authors can rely on, and there are two viable directions: full generic CLI assembly projection or a narrower system-prompt-addition-only contract.

options.title: Require full CLI assembly support
options.body: Generic CLI may advertise `assemble-before-prompt` only after it bootstraps first and projects assembled messages, system prompt additions, and relevant metadata into the CLI prompt path.

options.title: Create a narrower capability
options.body: Introduce and document a smaller capability for per-turn `systemPromptAddition` so engines requiring full assembled-message control continue to fail clearly on generic CLI.

options.title: Keep generic CLI unsupported
options.body: Leave generic CLI on bootstrap/after-turn/maintain only and keep docs and doctor behavior aligned with current host limitations.

recommendation.title: Require full CLI assembly support
recommendation.body: Generic CLI may advertise `assemble-before-prompt` only after it bootstraps first and projects assembled messages, system prompt additions, and relevant metadata into the CLI prompt path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about context-engine host semantics and Codex projection parity, which matches jalehman's recent merged work on the richer projection contract.
